caveat: Single successful case told by the evaluators themselves; the business case and the agonistic turn run together and are never separated.
source: Journal watch: Futures · full text read 28 Sep
title: Participatory co-production, agonistic pluralism, and transformation; Reflexively evaluating a technology for inclusive employment for people with a disability
why: A Dutch case where consensus-based co-production failed and the researchers turned adversarial — business case, then press, then parliament — and policy changed. The closest thing on your radar to a worked example of the structural-justice argument in 'Substrate Matters'.
